Title: Name company behind Puchong slaughterhouse raid, says Radzi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A member of parliament has called on the authorities to disclose the name of the company behind a
slaughterhouse raided
for breaching halal certification rules.
Putrajaya MP Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Jidin also called for the investigation into the company to be expedited.
"I am still waiting for the authorities to reveal the name of the company that runs the chicken processing facility raided in Puchong," he said in a Facebook post.
"Chickens were believed to have been processed by being submerged alive in scalding water until they died before being slaughtered."
Radzi said it was alarming that the poultry had reportedly been distributed to restaurants, grocery stores and supermarkets across Damansara, Bangi, Puchong, Cheras, Putra Perdana and Putrajaya.
"The public has a right to know the operator's name, company name, the exact location of the processing centre, the distributors, and where the chicken was supplied or sold to consumers," he said.
Yesterday, authorities raided the slaughterhouse in Puchong, seized more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken and arrested 12 foreign workers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: All 28 candidate nomination centres close at 10am
Article:
MELAKA: The nomination process for the Melaka election has been completed after all 28 nomination centres across the state closed at 10am.
The one-hour process for submitting nomination papers began at 9am, before the returning officers announced its closure at their respective centres.
Attention now turns to the official announcement of the list of candidates eligible to contest and the number of candidates vying for each state seat.
With nominations completed, the 14-day campaign period begins, as set by the Election Commission (EC), and will run until 11.59pm on Nov 13.
Checks at several nomination centres since early this morning found supporters accompanying their respective party candidates in an orderly manner.
The EC has set Nov 10 for early voting, while polling day is Nov 14.
A total of 687,697 voters are eligible to cast their ballots in the election, comprising 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
Article:
BRASILIA: Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said on Friday that he fled Brazil for the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country.
Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's election runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, secretly left Brazil on Tuesday and arrived in Florida aboard a private jet on Wednesday after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador.
"The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," the senator said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation.
In the video, he recounted how police informed him on Monday that his passports were being revoked as he left a visit to his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.
"With tears in his eyes, he told me: 'You know where they're going with this, don't you?'" he said of his father.
"I told him: 'Dad, I know... Now I know what I have to do,'" he recounted.
Although he gave no details of how he left the country, he said he and his wife made the decision "without anyone knowing" and urged people not to "point the finger at anyone".
US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei are under pressure to explain the involvement of the United States and Argentina in the senator's escape.
"I didn't leave Brazil, I left for Brazil," Flavio Bolsonaro said, alleging that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had made false accusations against him.
He also suggested there had been irregularities in the runoff, comparing them to "handball goals" that were not disallowed by VAR, without detailing what those irregularities might have been.
He also predicted that the economy would "go bust" under Lula and said he was willing to run for president again: "I'm not talking about 2030, I'm talking about before then."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man suffers broken leg in suspected hit-and-run over loan dispute in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A dispute over a loan is believed to have sparked a fight that led to a man being suspected of being hit by a car at Taman Pulai Utama, Skudai, yesterday.
Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said police received a report on the incident, which occurred in front of a supermarket, at 6.38pm.
"Initial investigations found that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a money loan between the two parties, who knew each other.
"The 35-year-old local man suffered a fracture to his right leg in the incident," he said in a statement today.
Following the incident, police arrested three people, comprising a man and two women aged between 34 and 53.
Radin Ramlan said police also seized a Proton Saga and were tracking down several others believed to be involved in the incident.
He said urine screening tests found all three suspects negative for drugs, while checks showed they had no criminal records.
"The victim was taken to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) and is reported to be in stable condition.
"The case is being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting and Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder," he said.
Earlier, a 26-second video showing a car driver suspected of hitting a motorcyclist who had already fallen before fleeing the scene went viral.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Tok Mat accompanies BN's Lendu candidate to nomination centre
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional candidate for the Lendu seat Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid arrived at the nomination centre for the Melaka election at 9.14am.
Abdul Hakim, who is also political secretary to Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, arrived at the Alor Gajah Youth Complex wearing a blue Baju Melayu and accompanied by BN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He is among eight new faces fielded by BN in the Nov 14 state election.
Meanwhile, Bersatu candidate Nazri Ramli arrived earlier, about 8.50am, wearing a red Baju Melayu and accompanied by the party's co-founder Datuk Seri Mohd Redzuan Md Yusof.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Sanusi turns up to back Pas candidate in Paya Rumput
Article:
MELAKA: Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor turned up at Hang Jebat Stadium today to accompany Pas candidate for the Paya Rumput seat Rafie Ahmad.
Sanusi, who is also PN election director, was seen alongside Rafie as Perikatan Nasional stepped up its campaign efforts in the constituency.
The seat allocation is part of the wider political cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Pas, which was formalised through a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on Oct 28.
The agreement was signed by Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, who is also Pas secretary-general, with BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi witnessing the ceremony.
Paya Rumput is among the seats attracting attention in the election after its incumbent, Datuk Rais Yasin of BN, opted not to defend the constituency and instead contest the Sungai Udang seat.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: 'Uncle Wong', 'Dak Nor' show up for BN's Duyong candidate's nomination
Article:
MELAKA: A lively atmosphere greeted incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem as he arrived at about 8.35am today at the Duyong state constituency nomination centre for the 16th Melaka state election.
Supporters of Mohd Noor Helmy, affectionately known as 'YB Duyong', began gathering around Dewan Kompleks Japerun Duyong as early as 8am, with 'Uncle Wong' and 'Dak Nor', two familiar faces in the constituency, joining the crowd.
UMNO secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki was also present at the nomination centre to accompany Mohd Noor Helmy.
Mohd Noor Helmy, 45, a former deputy state executive councillor for science, technology, innovation and digital communications, will face Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Poo Long Suan, who is also a committee member of the Melaka DAP Complaints Bureau.
Poo arrived at the nomination centre at 8.25am, accompanied by supporters waving flags and carrying banners.
In the 15th Melaka state election, Mohd Noor Helmy scored an upset victory over then-incumbent Damian Yeo Shen Li, winning by a slim majority of 200 votes.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hadi's presence boosts PN candidate's morale in Bukit Katil
Article:
MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif received a morale boost from the presence of Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang during his first appearance as a candidate.
Hadi arrived at 9.21am but did not join the march, while nearly 1,000 supporters, including those from Barisan Nasional (BN), accompanied Ridzuan to the nomination centre at Dewan Tun Ali.
Ridzuan, a Pas Hang Tuah Jaya division committee member, was accompanied by several coalition leaders, including PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir.
Also present were MP Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim and Alor Setar MP Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden.
As of 9.30am, the Bukit Katil state seat was set for a four-cornered contest.
Apart from Ridzuan, a former head of the Inspection and Legal Unit at the Melaka State Health Department, the seat will also be contested by two-term incumbent Adly Zahari, representing Pakatan Harapan (PH), Bersama candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin, 65.
The four candidates entered the hall to submit their nomination papers, with Adly leading the way at 9am.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Four parties bring colourful atmosphere to Klebang nomination centre
Article:
MELAKA: Supporters of four political parties turned up in large numbers at the Klebang Japerun Complex here today, creating a colourful atmosphere ahead of nomination for the Klebang seat.
Supporters of Pakatan Harapan, Barisan Nasional, Bersatu and Bersama began gathering as early as 7.30am, waving party flags and banners while wearing their respective party colours.
Chants and cheers could be heard from the various groups as they rallied behind their candidates, reflecting the enthusiasm of the respective party machinery ahead of the nomination process.
Several party leaders were also present to accompany their candidates, including MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong and Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli.
As of 8.30am, candidates from BN, Bersama and Bersatu had been seen entering the nomination centre.
MCA's Datuk Lim Ban Hong is defending the seat, while PH has named Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir as its candidate. Bersatu is fielding Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamed, while Bersama has named Young Jie Yu to contest the seat.
The atmosphere remained lively but orderly, with about 50 police personnel deployed from as early as 6am to maintain security around the complex.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Azman first to arrive at Paya Rumput nomination centre
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan candidate for the Paya Rumput seat Datuk Azman Abidin was the first to arrive at the nomination centre today, reaching Hang Jebat Stadium about 8.40am.
Azman, who is the political secretary to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, arrived ahead of the nomination process for the Paya Rumput seat in the 16th Melaka election.
He is among the candidates contesting the constituency, with Pas expected to field Rafiah Mat and Bersama naming Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar.
More than 200 PH supporters turned up for Azman as early as 7.30am
The supporters were accompanied by PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, who was present at Hang Jebat Stadium here, to lend his support to Azman as the coalition stepped up its campaign efforts in the constituency.
Azman had previously said he was contesting in Melaka because he wanted
to contribute to the state
, where his family has its roots.
Although he had never contested in an election before, he viewed the opportunity as a chance to serve the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Damansara Damai jewellery shop loses RM300,000 in robbery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man armed with a sharp weapon robbed a jewellery shop in Damansara Damai, Petaling Jaya, yesterday afternoon, resulting in losses estimated at RM300,000.
Petaling Jaya police chief assistant commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police were alerted to the robbery at 1.19pm.
"An investigation paper has been opened under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code, while efforts are underway to track down the suspect," he said.
Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters at 03-7966 2222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Sea of blue and red supporters gather at Tanjung Bidara
Article:
MELAKA: A sea of supporters dressed in blue and red gathered at Dewan Datuk KPT (B) Haji Ab Karim, Japerun Tanjung Bidara, here this morning as Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan candidates arrived for nomination for the Tanjung Bidara seat.
BN supporters, dressed in blue, began gathering as early as 7am before marching about 100 metres while waving party flags and chanting "blue wave" slogans as they accompanied caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh to the nomination centre.
Ab Rauf, who is also state BN chairman, arrived at 8.58am accompanied by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Dressed in a red Baju Melayu, PH candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri arrived at 8.20am accompanied by PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang.
The 36-year-old Masjid Tanah PKR pro-tem secretary was later seen entering the nomination centre at 9.06am.
The contest is expected to be a straight fight between Ab Rauf and Mohd Yunazri.
Tanjung Bidara is among the seats attracting attention in this state election, with Ab Rauf seeking to defend the seat he won in the 2021 Melaka election.
In the three-cornered contest, Ab Rauf secured 3,559 votes to defeat his challengers, Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin and Zainal Hassan, with a majority of 364 votes.
According to the Election Commission, Tanjung Bidara has 15,003 registered voters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Party cheers, chants mark nomination day in Machap Jaya
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Chants of "Reformasi!" and "Melaka rumah kita!" echoed around the Japerun Machap Jaya Complex as Pakatan Harapan (PH) supporters accompanied the coalition's candidate, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, to the nomination centre for the 16th Melaka state election.
The group of PH supporters, dressed in red and carrying party flags, arrived at the venue at about 8.25am alongside their candidate, who was wearing a grey baju kurung.
Also accompanying the PH candidate were PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, PKR Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek and PKR International Bureau director Dr Maszlee Malik.
Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem was accompanied by MCA secretary-general Datuk Chong Sin Woon.
Meanwhile, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate Prasanth Kumar Brakasam was also accompanied by supporters dressed in yellow and carrying yellow flags, reflecting the party's signature colour.
Prasanth, who wore a yellow batik shirt, was accompanied by supporters chanting "Ayuh Bersama! Machap Jaya Prasanth!" as they marched towards the nomination centre.
About 9am, PH candidate Ginie Lim was the first to enter the nomination centre to submit her nomination papers, followed by Prasanth of Bersama and Ngwe of BN, who was wearing a white shirt.
A check around the Japerun Machap Jaya Complex found that policemen had been deployed to manage traffic and maintain order in the vicinity of the nomination centre.
Policemen and Election Commission (EC) officers were also stationed at the main entrance to control the movement of people entering the premises.
Media practitioners began gathering around the nomination centre as early as 7am to cover the nomination process.
The Machap Jaya state seat is expected to see a three-cornered contest in the 16th Melaka state election, with the incumbent facing two challengers from PH and Bersama.
Ngwe will face former Machap Jaya assemblyman Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin (PH) and former special officer to the Chief Minister Prasanth Kumar Brakasam (Bersama).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A different kind of buzz at Bukit Katil nomination centre
Article:
MELAKA: A nomination centre is usually abuzz with political supporters rallying behind their candidates, but the scene at Dewan Tun Ali in Bukit Katil today offered a different spectacle, with a children's football match and preparations for a wedding reception adding to the activity.
While candidates and supporters gathered for the nomination process for the 16th Melaka state election, children were busy chasing the ball on the football field, while a marquee was being set up nearby for a wedding reception.
The unusual mix of activities brought together three very different occasions at one location - the political contest for voters' support, the children's pursuit of victory on the football field and preparations to celebrate a newlywed couple.
The football match was part of the Rimau Melaka Super League, involving 12 teams in the Under-8 and Under-10 categories.
Crew assistant Afiz Abdul Ghani said the league, which involved a total of 35 teams, had been running for the past three months and was scheduled to conclude on Nov 15.
"The teams are from Melaka, with a few from Johor, and the league champions will represent Melaka at the national level, " he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, preparations for the wedding reception continued with a large tent set up near the nomination centre, adding to the unusual scene on nomination day.
Candidates and supporters of the contesting parties were expected to arrive from 8.30am, ahead of the nomination process scheduled from 9am to 10am.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 14 as polling day, while early voting will take place on Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police liaising with Pakistani authorities over 130 Malaysians detained in scam raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is liaising with Pakistani authorities through the Foreign Ministry to obtain further details about a raid on a suspected cyber scam centre in Rawalpindi, Pakistan.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the matter had been referred to the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director following the detention of 130 Malaysians in the raid.
"Some (of the Malaysians arrested) have valid visas, while others have overstayed their visas.
"We still need assistance from the Pakistani authorities to obtain all the relevant details," he said after attending an appreciation dinner organised by the Malaysian Ex-Police Association last night.
Khalid said he had instructed the CCID to maintain contact with Pakistani authorities and did not rule out the possibility of sending officers to the country.
On the identities of those detained, he said police had yet to receive a complete list from Pakistani authorities.
"We have not received the full list of names, but the Pakistani authorities have informed us that those detained are holders of Malaysian passports.
"They come from various races and we will obtain further details as soon as possible," he said.
Earlier, Pakistani media reported that the country's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) had
raided a call centre
at KASA Tower, Bahria Town Phase VIII, Rawalpindi, over suspected cyber scam activities targeting Malaysians.
According to news portal ProPakistani on Wednesday, the syndicate made calls posing as bank customer service officers before contacting victims through Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) applications.
Victims were told that suspicious transactions had been detected in their bank accounts. Their calls were then transferred to other individuals posing as Malaysian police officers.
Some of the suspects wore police uniforms and used backgrounds resembling police offices during video calls to make their claims appear more convincing.
Victims were threatened with allegations of money laundering or other criminal activities and pressured into transferring money.
The proceeds were believed to have been channelled through Touch 'n Go eWallet before being converted into cryptocurrency.
The report also said the syndicate was believed to be run by a Malaysian national based in Cambodia, with the assistance of supervisors and call centre managers in Pakistan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN, PH leaders rally behind candidates in Ayer Molek
Article:
MELAKA: Two leaders from parties in the unity government arrived at the Ayer Molek Japerun Complex here to accompany and show their support for their respective candidates contesting the Ayer Molek seat on nomination day today.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, who is also Investment, Trade and Industry Minister, arrived about 8.30am to accompany Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali.
Ridhwan is the son of Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
Meanwhile, PKR communications director and Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim arrived to accompany Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar, who is the Melaka PKR Youth chief.
[[nid:1567418]]
The Ayer Molek seat is expected to see a straight fight between Ridhwan and Hakimin. In the 2021 state election, BN won the seat with its candidate, Datuk Rahmad Mariman, securing a majority of 2,802 votes.
According to the Election Commission, Ayer Molek has about 24,600 registered voters.
Ridhwan, who is also Hang Tuah Jaya Umno division chief, previously contested the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary seat in the 15th General Election but lost to Adam Adli. Hakimin, meanwhile, is a new face.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Amirudin joins over 200 PH supporters to support Azman
Article:
MELAKA: More than 200 Pakatan Harapan (PH) supporters gathered in Paya Rumput today to back the coalition's candidate, Datuk Azman Abidin, in the 16th Melaka state election.
The supporters were accompanied by PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, who was present at Hang Jebat Stadium to lend his support to Azman as the coalition geared up for its campaign efforts.
Jun Lye Chye Yoon, 51, who has lived in Paya Rumput for 18 years, said she trusted Azman because of his close working relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
She said the constituency needed a representative with the level of access and experience that Azman could bring, particularly given his role working closely with the prime minister.
Another supporter, research officer Yogeswary S. Veloo, 55, said she had seen Azman work first-hand and believed he understood his responsibilities and knew what needed to be done for the people.
She said her confidence in him was based on his work ethic and ability to carry out his duties.
Azman, who is also the political secretary to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, is contesting the N.13 Paya Rumput seat in an expected three-cornered fight against Pas candidate Rafie Ahmad and Bersama's Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar.
He previously said his decision to contest in Melaka was driven by a desire to contribute to the state, which has links to his family's roots.
Although he had never contested an election before, he viewed the opportunity as a chance to serve the state.
In the 2021 state election, BN's Datuk Rais Yasin retained Paya Rumput with a majority of 629 votes after securing 6,830 votes.
PH's Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin came second with 6,201 votes, while PN's Muhammad Faris Izwan Mazlan garnered 3,972 votes.
Rais, however, will not defend Paya Rumput in this election and has instead been fielded in Sungai Udang.
Polling is scheduled for Nov 14, while early voting will take place on Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Bersama's Aliza arrives first as Adly Zahari set to defend Bukit Katil
Article:
BUKIT KATIL: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate for the N17 Bukit Katil seat, Dr Aliza Che Amran, arrived at the nomination centre at Dewan Tun Ali.
She was the first candidate to arrive ahead of the nomination process, which is scheduled to begin at 9am.
The state seat is expected to see a three-cornered contest.

Title: Sabah public bus ridership jumps 208pct in two months
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Ridership on Kota Kinabalu's public bus service has surged by 208 per cent in two months, said Sabah Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (CVLB) chairman Datuk Phoong Jin Zhe.
The number of passengers increased from about 194,000 in August to 598,054 in October.
"These figures are very encouraging and prove that the people of Sabah genuinely need a better public transport system. When services are provided well, people will use them.
"Our goal is very clear, to make public transport an easy, safe, comfortable and accessible option for all segments of society.
"We want more people to be able to travel to hospitals, schools, workplaces and community centres without having to rely too heavily on private vehicles," he said in a statement.
The BAS.MY service, also known as the "Pink Bus", was officially launched a few months ago and covers stops at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I and II, as well as Kota Kinabalu International Airport.
He said the board also aimed to add stops in strategic areas such as Luyang Health Clinic, Likas Hospital, Tanjung Aru and Kepayan Ridge, based on public demand.
However, implementation would require amendments to the procurement contract and approval from the Transport Ministry and Finance Ministry.
Meanwhile, a total of 1,106 school bus, hire-car and taxi drivers throughout Sabah have been approved to receive a one-off RM1,000 assistance payment.
The Pink Bus service operates daily from 5.30am, with buses running at intervals of approximately 15 to 30 minutes.
Passengers can check bus schedules and track bus locations in real time through the LUGO mobile application.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Different party colours, one breakfast table
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Supporters of Barisan Nasional (BN), Pakatan Harapan (PH), Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Bersama put their political differences aside to share a breakfast stall today.

The atmosphere was enlivened by a convoy of vehicles flying yellow flags in support of Bersama.

Ngwe will be challenged by former Machap Jaya assemblyman Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin (PH) and former special officer to the chief minister Prasanth Kumar Brakasam (Bersama).

Title: Start small and save early with PTPTN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parents should start saving for their children's education early, even if they can only afford small amounts, to prepare for future higher education costs.
As the world marks World Savings Day today, the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) is encouraging families to make saving a regular habit and plan ahead for their children's education.
PTPTN chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim said the occasion was an important reminder that financial well-being began with disciplined saving and careful planning.
She said parents should not wait until their children were approaching university age before setting aside money for higher education.
"When it comes to education, the preparation period is long, but time passes quickly. That is why I always encourage parents to start saving when their children are still young, according to their financial means.
"There is no need to wait until they have a substantial amount of money. What matters is getting started, making saving a routine and increasing savings when they can afford to do so," she said.
Norliza said the value of saving should not be measured solely by the amount accumulated, but also by the discipline and consistency developed along the way.
Small, regular contributions could help families build financial confidence while teaching children about money management and responsibility.
World Savings Day is observed annually on Oct 31. It was established following the first International Savings Bank Congress in Milan, Italy, in 1924, and was first celebrated the following year.
Norliza said the occasion should encourage Malaysians to reassess their spending habits and recognise savings as an important foundation for financial resilience.
"World Savings Day is more than just an annual event. It serves as a reminder that savings are an important foundation for a family's financial well-being and resilience," she said.
Making education savings affordable
Norliza said rising living costs could make it difficult for some parents to prioritise education savings, particularly when household incomes were committed to food, housing and schooling expenses.
However, families should not feel pressured to save beyond their means. Instead, parents should prioritise essential household needs and gradually set aside whatever they could afford.
"My advice is to prioritise the family's basic needs first and, when there is room in the budget, start saving for education with a small amount. It is perfectly fine if the amount varies from month to month," she said.
Setting realistic targets and including education savings in the family budget could help parents develop a sustainable approach to financial planning.
Norliza also encouraged parents to involve children in saving activities to strengthen financial literacy at home.
When parents demonstrate responsible financial habits, children are more likely to understand the importance of planning ahead and managing money wisely.
Simpan SSPN supports long-term planning
PTPTN continues to promote Simpan SSPN as a way for parents and guardians to prepare for their children's higher education expenses.
Norliza said the scheme allowed families to choose options that suited their financial circumstances while encouraging disciplined education planning.
Simpan SSPN offers several benefits, including income tax relief on savings of up to RM8,000 annually, takaful protection for depositors and a free Matching Grant of up to RM10,000 per family for eligible households.
Other benefits include competitive dividend rates, government-guaranteed savings and Shariah compliance.
Norliza said these features provided additional incentives for families to build financial resources for their children's education.
PTPTN also wants to change the perception that higher education financing should only be considered after students receive university or other higher education institution offers.
"Rather than seeking financing only when their children receive an offer to pursue further studies, parents are encouraged to plan their savings early so that they have better financial options," she said.
Homemaker Jayaranee Jayachandran, who has been saving through Simpan SSPN Prime for her child since 2009, said the government's guarantee was among the main reasons she chose the scheme.
"I chose to save through Simpan SSPN because it is an education savings platform guaranteed by the Malaysian government.
"I started saving in 2009," she said.
Jayaranee said she valued the income tax relief and dividend rates, which she considered more attractive than those offered by financial institutions.
She added that the flexibility to withdraw savings was another important factor behind her decision.
[[nid:1567345]]
World Savings Day
In conjunction with World Savings Day, PTPTN is organising its ninth Simpan SSPN Savings Month, or Bulan Menabung Simpan SSPN (BMS 2026), to raise public awareness of education savings.
Running from Sept 25 to Nov 1, the programme carries the theme "Under the Sea" and the tagline "Be Your Child's Superhero".
Norliza said the theme drew inspiration from underwater exploration, symbolising the journey of developing saving habits, managing finances and fulfilling children's educational aspirations.
Through promotional activities, information-sharing sessions and community programmes, PTPTN aims to provide parents, guardians and young Malaysians with practical information about education savings.
"Programmes such as this are important because awareness alone is not enough without action.
"We want the public to take concrete steps, whether by starting to save, adding to their existing savings or encouraging family members to develop saving habits," she said.
Norliza said the programme provided opportunities for the public to engage directly with PTPTN, seek clarification about education savings and make informed financial decisions.
Campaign rewards encourage regular savings
Beyond BMS 2026, PTPTN is strengthening its promotional efforts through the Cabutan Simpan SSPN 2026, which offers prizes worth nearly RM1.9 million to 1,060 winners.
The year-long campaign, which ends on Dec 31, features four special prize draws: the WOW! Plus Loyalty 2026 Draw (annual category), WOW! Plus Series Draw, Simpan SSPN Baru Slay! Draw and Prime Bonanza Draw.
Norliza said the initiatives were designed to encourage more Malaysians to start saving while rewarding existing depositors for their continued commitment.
[[nid:1567344]]
Digital services make saving more accessible
PTPTN is also expanding its digital services to make education savings more convenient.
Through the myPTPTN application, users can open Simpan SSPN accounts, make additional deposits and manage their savings digitally.
The corporation is also using mass media, social media and outreach programmes to communicate the scheme's benefits to a wider audience.
Norliza said these efforts reflected PTPTN's commitment to strengthening financial literacy and encouraging responsible financial behaviour among Malaysians.
Building a savings culture for future generations
Television and film producer Nasreen Ngasri, who saves through Simpan SSPN for her child, said the scheme had helped parents plan financially for their children's education.
She said she began saving for her child at a young age, believing early preparation could ease the financial burden of further studies.
"I would like to thank PTPTN for providing the Simpan SSPN platform, which gives parents the opportunity to plan their finances and save for their children's educational future.
"I personally started saving for my child when my child was young because I believe that saving early can help ease the financial burden when the time comes for further studies," she said.
Nasreen said attractive dividends and the convenience of managing savings through a user-friendly application had made the process easier.
She encouraged parents not to underestimate the importance of small but regular contributions.
"My advice to parents is to seize the opportunity to start saving through Simpan SSPN because every amount saved, no matter how small, is very meaningful for their children's future.
"What matters is discipline and consistency in saving, especially as children grow older and their educational needs increase," she said.
Nasreen said parents should also lead by example by demonstrating good saving habits.
"When children see their parents practising the habit of saving, they will also learn to appreciate money, be thrifty and plan their finances from a young age.
"Do not wait until you have a lot of money to start saving. Start now, save consistently and build a more carefully planned educational future for your children," she said.
Meanwhile, Norliza encouraged existing Simpan SSPN depositors to continue saving consistently and urged Malaysians to consider opening at least one Simpan SSPN account per family.
PTPTN, she said, would continue supporting access to higher education through savings, financing and financial education.
"Parents should make education savings a priority, even if they start with a small amount, because the discipline practised today can open up more opportunities for their children in the future," she said.
Norliza said cultivating a strong savings culture required continued commitment from families and institutions, with financial literacy playing an important role in helping Malaysians make informed decisions.
"Let us use World Savings Day and BMS 2026 as an opportunity to make saving and the responsibility of building an education fund a lasting culture that we pass down to future generations," she said.
For more information on Simpan SSPN, and PTPTN services, visit www.ptptn.gov.my or use the myPTPTN application.

Title: Malaysia may hit four-year growth high as HSBC lifts 2026 forecast [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy could post its strongest annual growth in four years after HSBC raised its 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to 5.5 per cent from 5.2 per cent, a revision that economists say is plausible.
HSBC cited Malaysia's sustained strong momentum, backed by robust domestic demand and a surge in electronics exports.
If realised, the expansion would be the fastest since 2022, when the economy rebounded by 8.7 per cent following the Covid-19 pandemic.
Setting aside the post-pandemic rebound, it would be the strongest annual growth in nine years, since 2017, when the economy expanded by about 5.9 per cent.
HSBC said the upgrade followed Malaysia's better-than-expected advance GDP growth estimate of 5.3 per cent for the third quarter (Q3).
The bank also raised its Q4 growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 4.7 per cent, suggesting that economic momentum would continue through the end of the year.
Economist Geoffrey Williams said a growth of 5.5 per cent or more was realistic and should continue into next year.
Sunway University economics professor Dr Yeah Kim Leng described the forecast as plausible and well-grounded, although it sits above consensus.
"The economy grew 5.5 per cent across the first three quarters, and with momentum holding into Q4 underpinned by resilient private consumption and investment, low inflation and a record electronics export surge, there is a strong chance the full-year outturn will indeed reach 5.5 per cent," Yeah said.
However, he cautioned that base effects and a normalisation of external demand in the final quarter could temper this outlook slightly.
Additionally, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said 5.5 per cent was achievable, considering the strength of the Malaysian economy in the first nine months of the year.
"Malaysia also beat market expectations," HSBC added, referring to the Q3 performance.
It said Malaysia was benefiting from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, with electronics exports growing at a record 60 per cent year-on-year on a three-month moving average basis.
HSBC identified Malaysia and Singapore as Asean's two main beneficiaries of AI-related demand, while the country's position as a net energy exporter also provided an advantage amid elevated commodity prices.
"While it is tempting to attribute Malaysia's outperformance just to trade, it is a sustained broad-based story," it said.
The bank said private consumption and investment remained key drivers of growth, supported by relatively low inflation, government subsidies and continued infrastructure development.
Consumers were also better positioned to spend than their regional peers, with Malaysia recording Asean's lowest inflation rate.
Headline inflation averaged 1.8 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, while core inflation remained around 2 per cent.
HSBC attributed the subdued inflation partly to government subsidies, particularly for RON95 petrol, which remains priced at RM1.99 per litre under the subsidised scheme, subject to a monthly quota of 300 litres.
Investment growth, meanwhile, has moderated to single digits after two consecutive years of double-digit expansion.
"The infrastructure push continues," HSBC said, although it noted that several projects were approaching their operational phase.
Malaysia has also become more selective in approving private data centre investments due to environmental and regulatory concerns.
Yeah said slower investment would soften growth rather than cause a sharp slowdown.
Investment accounts for a significant but not overly dominant share of the economy at 23 per cent of GDP, of which private investment contributed 19 percentage points in the first half of 2026.
Despite the stronger growth outlook, HSBC expects Bank Negara Malaysia to maintain the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent at its Nov 5 monetary policy meeting.
HSBC said Bank Negara had adopted a slightly more hawkish tone in September, but underlying inflation remained too subdued to warrant an immediate interest rate increase.
It noted that the central bank had removed the word "appropriate" from its description of the monetary policy stance, suggesting greater flexibility for future policy normalisation rather than a commitment to a fixed cycle of rate increases.
"We do not believe current underlying inflation is strong enough to trigger Bank Negara to hike imminently," HSBC said.
Williams agreed that Bank Negara would likely hold rates, while Yeah said a hold was expected given contained inflation and firm growth momentum supporting a steady stance, although the meeting could deliver hawkish signals.
However, Afzanizam said a rate hike in November was possible, as Bank Negara may want to normalise its monetary policy stance in line with higher economic growth and a stable inflation environment.
"Last year, when Bank Negara cut OPR rates, it was done on a basis to pre-empt any potential slowdown following the US tariff shocks.
"Meaning, clearly, the current growth trajectory suggests such policy support needs to be adjusted by removing some of the policy accommodation," he added.
HSBC expects Bank Negara to raise the OPR by 25 basis points to three per cent in the first quarter of 2027, describing the potential increase as a pre-emptive move towards policy normalisation rather than a response to rising inflation.
Yeah said such a pre-emptive move was expected early next year, but remained data-dependent, particularly on domestic core inflation and growth momentum.
Meanwhile, Afzanizam said the strong performance in the first nine months would result in a higher base for 2026, which could cause growth to moderate in 2027.
HSBC expects Malaysia's economic growth to moderate to five per cent in 2027 and 4.7 per cent in 2028.

Title: PH-Bersatu clashes in Melaka could benefit BN, PN – Analysts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan and Bersatu contesting against each other in four Melaka constituencies could benefit Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional.
Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Prof Dr Azizuddin Mohd Sani said the absence of a formal electoral pact between PH and Bersatu meant multi-cornered contests were to be expected.
He said the outcome would inevitably lead to vote-splitting, potentially benefiting BN and PN.
"Based on what had happened in Johor and Negri Sembilan, it favours BN and PN. Thus, in Melaka, it will suit BN and PN to win again," he said.
Four state constituencies will see straight or multi-cornered contests between PH and Bersatu in the Melaka election.
The seats are Ayer Keroh, Klebang, Gadek and Pengkalan Batu, all of which PH will be defending in the Nov 14 polls.
Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) political analyst Prof Dr Mujibu Abd Muis said the overlapping contests demonstrated that parties could function as parliamentary partners while remaining direct electoral rivals.
"This highlights the distinct calculations at play in Malaysian politics. While federal-level cooperation (the signing of the Confidence and Supply Agreement) ensures governance stability, state-level dynamics are driven by independent electoral interests and ambitions," he said.
Mujibu said the bigger challenge would be whether both sides could maintain cooperation in Putrajaya while campaigning against each other in Melaka without allowing local political hostility to undermine future ties.
"Competing directly for the same seats will complicate efforts to build mutual trust and hamper the development of a sustainable long-term relationship," he said.
On the electoral implications, he identified vote fragmentation, deteriorating grassroots relations and declining voter confidence as three key concerns.
He said direct competition in overlapping constituencies could fragment votes, although the extent of the impact would depend on local demographics, candidate profiles and previous voting patterns.
The presence of other parties like Gerakan and Bersama, in multi-cornered contests such as Ayer Keroh would further complicate the electoral calculations.
"To maintain credibility ahead of the 16th general election, any future cooperation must move beyond loose parliamentary agreements and clearly define common objectives, political boundaries and shared responsibilities," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Top EU diplomat says Lavrov presented 'lies' at G20 talks
Article:
ATLANTA: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov presented "lies" during G20 talks on the Ukraine conflict, the EU's foreign policy chief told AFP on Friday, accusing Moscow of being unprepared for peace negotiations.
"We were talking about the big geopolitical crises, including Ukraine, and we were able to address Sergei Lavrov head-on with this," Kaja Kallas said on the sidelines of a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Georgia.
"Of course, he put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives that we were also able to then rebuke," she added.
Lavrov's appearance at the two-day gathering of foreign ministers had fuelled tensions with European representatives while highlighting warmer US-Russia ties.
It also comes ahead of fresh negotiations expected between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington in November.
But Russia does not appear ready to move ahead with peace talks, Kallas said.
"Even if they would have said this in words, their deeds tell something else," she said. "July, August and September have been the deadliest months for civilians in Ukraine."
"They should show with their deeds that they are ready to negotiate, but they are clearly, clearly not," she added.
She also called for continued pressure on Moscow, particularly to secure a ceasefire in the Black Sea.
Earlier on Friday, a traditional family photo of G20 ministers was called off, with a diplomatic source telling AFP that some European officials had declined to appear alongside Lavrov.
Asked about the cancellation, Kallas said that when Russia started the war against Ukraine, European officials had agreed not to normalise its presence at international platforms.
"We haven't changed our policies," she said.
A US official said the photograph was cancelled to avoid allowing "a ceremonial photo opportunity to become a diplomatic distraction".
Kallas expressed regret that "at the moment, we are not sending very clear messages".
"For us, it is very clear that the pressure should be on the aggressor to stop this war," she said of the Ukraine conflict.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 16th Melaka election kicks off with nomination process today [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: The 16th Melaka election officially begins today, with the nomination process taking place simultaneously at 28 nomination centres across the state from 9am.
Prospective candidates have until 10am to submit their nomination papers to the election returning officers, before the list of eligible candidates is officially announced.
Following the announcement, the contest for the people's mandate will enter a 14-day campaigning period, which runs until 11.59pm on Nov 13, as stipulated by the Election Commission (EC).
The EC has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
It said 189 nomination forms had been purchased as of Thursday night, with 45 prospective candidates having paid their deposits.
EC statistics show that 687,697 people are eligible to vote in the state election, including 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 members of the armed forces and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast clear skies across the state in the morning, setting the scene for nomination day.
The Melaka State Legislative Assembly was officially dissolved with effect from Sept 23, following the consent of Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the 2021 Melaka election, Barisan Nasional secured 21 of the 28 seats, allowing it to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional took two.

Title: E-waste trade driven by value of precious metals in discarded devices
Article:
PORT KLANG: A discarded computer or electronic device may have reached the end of its useful life, but the materials inside it can still command a price.
That commercial value is one of the economic drivers of the international e-waste trade.
Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said printed circuit boards (PCBs) could contain precious metals, including gold, silver and palladium.
Also found in PCBs are tin, aluminium, nickel, zinc and iron. Lead is also among the materials identified.
Department of Environment figures estimate that an e-waste consignment weighing 15 to 20 tonnes can be worth US$4,000 to US$8,000. It  puts  disposal costs at RM500 to RM3,000 per tonne.
Nik Ezanee said the figures highlighted the economics of e-waste: valuable materials could be recovered and sold, while disposing of the remaining waste incurred a cost.
"This means obsolete electronics cannot simply be regarded as worthless.
"The commercial incentive lies in extracting materials that still have value, particularly precious metals, while the remaining waste must still be handled and disposed of properly."
He said controlling the movement of e-waste at the border was only part of the equation.
"We must also ensure that the recovery, processing and disposal of the material are carried out through legitimate channels."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Following the money trail behind Malaysia's e-waste trade
Article:
PORT KLANG: Authorities are tracing the financial and physical networks behind Malaysia's e-waste trade, with hundreds of abandoned containers linked to anti-money laundering investigations and enforcement teams targeting suspected illegal storage facilities inland.
Of the 1,257 containers abandoned at Port Klang in 2024 and 2025, 772 were linked to police investigations, 375 were handled by the Customs Department and 112 by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA).
The containers held an estimated 31,475 tonnes of electronic waste.
MCBA Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said police were investigating 772 containers under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
The investigations could help establish the businesses and players behind the shipments, including the roles of importers, consignees and shipping agents, as well as the circumstances surrounding the abandonment of the containers.
He said information shared between MCBA and Bukit Aman, particularly the Internal Security and Public Order Department and Anti-Money Laundering Unit, had yielded results.
He said MCBA had also passed intelligence to the Internal Security and Public Order Department through its deputy director, Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi, to facilitate enforcement against premises suspected of illegally storing or handling e-waste after it entered the country.
"He has been proactive in conducting operations based on intelligence from us."
"In one operation, 25 foreigners were detained in a raid on a suspected illegal e-waste storage facility in Kapar.
"Items worth about RM3.1 million were seized."
Information from the MCBA Port Klang joint task force showed that offences involve the Environmental Quality Act 1974, Immigration Act 1959/63 and licensing regulations under the Klang Royal City Council.
Nik Ezanee said the operation illustrated the wider enforcement challenge once e-waste moved beyond the country's entry points.
"Investigators must not only identify who brought these shipments into Malaysia, but also the premises and operators involved in storing, dismantling or processing e-waste illegally.
"Authorities need to trace both sides of the trade, the financial transactions and companies behind the shipments, and the movement of the material once it reaches Malaysia."
He said establishing those connections could prove crucial in preventing another accumulation of unwanted e-waste.
"Clearing abandoned containers tackles the immediate problem at the port.
"Following the money trail and shutting down illegal facilities can help authorities disrupt the network that allows the trade to operate in the first place."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Russia uncompromising as Rubio hosts G20 talks in shadow of conflicts
Article:
ATLANTA: Russia showed no sign on Friday of softening its stance on Kyiv as G20 foreign ministers opened talks in the United States, with the wars in Ukraine and Iran deepening rifts between members of the sprawling forum.
Sharp disagreements emerged around the table, with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accusing Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov of presenting "lies" on issues such as the conflict in Ukraine.
"He put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives" that Europeans were able to push back on, Kallas told AFP.
European officials also sought to put more pressure on Moscow, particularly to secure a ceasefire in the Black Sea, a key agricultural export corridor.
Lavrov, in turn, was "quite provocative" in his remarks, a European diplomatic source said.
At a press conference, Lavrov criticised Europeans for their "arrogant boycott" while praising the willingness of US President Donald Trump's administration to engage with Moscow.
Plans for a traditional family photo of G20 ministers were called off after some European officials objected to appearing alongside Lavrov, a diplomatic source told AFP.
European leaders have opted not to appear in photographs with Russian delegations at other G20 meetings this year, as fighting continues more than four years after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
A US official said the photograph was cancelled to avoid allowing "a ceremonial photo opportunity to become a diplomatic distraction".
The gathering in Atlanta, taking place just days before the US midterm elections, sets the stage for a G20 leaders' summit at Trump's Doral resort in Miami in December.
But it also comes as global energy prices have rocketed since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February. Teheran retaliated by choking off the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for oil and gas transit.
Even as the United States seeks to focus on economic growth, trade imbalances and supply chain challenges — covering areas such as energy and critical minerals — few breakthroughs are expected.
Instead of a final declaration, the two days of talks are expected to conclude on Saturday with a chair's summary drafted by the United States.
'Decent talk'
Still, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told an opening plenary that the world faces a critical "moment of choosing" as it grapples with "interconnected economic and geopolitical crises".
He urged the Group of 20 forum — which includes China, France, Germany, India, Japan and Russia — to work together against threats such as strains on global energy and food supply chains, and to uphold freedom of navigation.
Rubio spoke briefly with Lavrov on the sidelines of the G20 meeting, with the Russian minister saying both sides had a "decent talk".
Moscow has been shunned by most of the West since it invaded Ukraine, and Lavrov himself remains under international sanctions.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said that "there is no normality with Russia" and pledged to again "call on Russia to finally accept Ukraine's offer of a ceasefire, starting in the Black Sea".
Rubio's interactions with Lavrov in Atlanta are being closely watched as Washington pursues diplomacy on Ukraine while seeking Moscow's cooperation in reining in fuel prices, a key campaign issue in the US midterm elections.
Lavrov's G20 appearance comes ahead of fresh negotiations expected between Moscow, Kyiv and Washington in November.
Analysts say his presence is not surprising, as Washington has welcomed Russian officials to this year's G20 events while excluding fellow member South Africa.
Trump has also invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to Florida in December and eased some sanctions on Moscow while touting a deal for Russia to sell diesel as prices soared, squeezing Americans.
Another issue key to the US agenda is freedom of navigation.
A US State Department official flagged "shared resolve to confront urgent crises and keep critical sea lanes open to commerce without threats or tolls".
But the possibility of further escalation in the Middle East is mounting, with Trump signalling he could attack Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia widens e-waste crackdown beyond Port Klang [WATCH]
Article:
PORT KLANG: More than 31,000 tonnes of electronic waste packed into 1,257 containers were abandoned at Port Klang, prompting a multi-agency crackdown that has expanded beyond the port to suspected illegal storage and processing facilities inland.
What began as an operation to clear the backlog has evolved into a wider enforcement effort involving re-exports, investigations, licence action and raids on premises suspected of handling e-waste illegally.
Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) Port Klang joint task force records show that the 1,257 containers were abandoned in 2024 and 2025, with their contents estimated to weigh 31,475 tonnes.
MCBA Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the operation involved close cooperation between enforcement agencies to clear the backlog and take action against those responsible.
"Of the 1,257 containers, 772 were linked to police investigations under anti-money laundering laws, 375 were handled by the Customs Department and 112 by MCBA," he said in an exclusive interview recently.
The three-phase operation has shipped out 647 containers containing an estimated 16,177 tonnes of e-waste. The task force puts the operation at 51 per cent complete.
The third phase, from Oct 1 to Dec 31, covers the remaining 578 containers, Nik Ezanee said.
But the operation is no longer limited to Port Klang.
Enforcement teams have also taken action against suspected illegal e-waste operations outside the port, including a storage facility in Kapar where 25 foreigners were detained and items worth RM3.1 million were seized.
The raid underscored the challenge of tracking imported waste after it enters the country.
Nik Ezanee said enforcement efforts must also target businesses, storage facilities and processing centres that receive and handle e-waste illegally.
The financial incentive behind the trade adds to the challenge, as discarded electronic equipment can contain recoverable materials, including precious metals.
Nik Ezanee said clearing the existing backlog addressed only part of the problem.
"The bigger task is identifying those responsible for bringing the material into Malaysia and shutting down the channels that allow unwanted electronic waste to be imported, abandoned, stored or processed illegally.
"With another 578 containers scheduled to be dealt with under phase three, the operation is entering its final and largest stage."
The success of the crackdown will be measured not merely by how many containers leave Port Klang, but by whether authorities can prevent another backlog.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST CRIME WATCH: Dead baby in bin, another abandoned; murder probe and custody death draw scrutiny [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: One baby was found dead in a rubbish bin while another was found abandoned beneath a staircase. Both cases were reported in Kuala Lumpur.
In Penampang, Sabah, a suspect was arrested in connection with a 17-year-old murder case.
In Kota Tinggi, Johor, a 68-year-old Felda settler was found axed to death.
A death in custody at the Cheras district police headquarters also drew the attention of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Below are some of the major crimes reported this week.
BABY GIRL FOUND DEAD IN BANGSAR RUBBISH BIN
The body of a baby girl, believed to be about seven months old, was
found in a rubbish bin
at a waste-disposal site in Bangsar on Oct 23.
Brickfields district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the discovery was made by an Alam Flora worker.
The body, measuring approximately 28cm, was taken to the Forensics Unit at Hospital Kuala Lumpur for a post-mortem examination to establish the cause of death.
On Oct 24, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that two foreigners, a 23-year-old man and a 31-year-old woman, had been detained near the scene to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 318 of the Penal Code, which concerns the secret disposal of the body of a child, whether the child dies before, during or after birth. Investigators are seeking to establish the baby's identity, the cause of death and how the body came to be discarded.
BABY BOY ABANDONED IN A BOX
A one-month-old
baby boy was found alive
in a box beneath the staircase of an apartment block at Desa Satu, Desa Aman Puri, Jalan Puri Kepong, on Oct 22.
Gombak district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ibrahim Husin said the infant was in good health and had been admitted to hospital for observation.
Initial reports did not establish the identity of the person responsible or the circumstances surrounding the case.
It is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code, which concerns the exposure or abandonment of a child under 12 by a parent or person having care of the child, with the intention of wholly abandoning the child. Police have appealed for information to help identify the person responsible.
PENAMPANG MURDER COLD CASE, SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER 17 YEARS
Police arrested a 42-year-old man on Oct 22 in connection with the murder of a man in Beverly Hills, Penampang, on April 11, 2009.
The suspect was detained by officers from the Penampang district police headquarters at a house in Kolombong, Inanam.
Acting Penampang police chief ASP Arisanti Aziz announced the arrest on Oct 24, describing it as part of police efforts to track down people suspected of involvement in serious crimes.
The arrest came more than 17 years after the murder. However, the report did not identify the victim, detail the circumstances of the killing or explain what evidence led investigators to the suspect.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. The arrest marks a significant development in the long-running investigation.
FELDA SETTLER MURDERED IN KOTA TINGGI
A 68-year-old Felda settler was
found dead with slash wounds
to his head and both arms at Felda Lok Heng Selatan, Kota Tinggi, on Oct 26.
Residents had reportedly seen a man behaving aggressively while carrying an axe in the area. The victim was found lying by the roadside, and medical personnel from the nearby Bukit Waha Health Clinic pronounced him dead.
[[nid:1567301]]
Police arrested a 41-year-old man at an oil palm plantation the following day. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police seized an axe and a motorcycle believed to be connected to the incident.
Police checks found that the suspect had six previous criminal and drug-related records. However, the motive for the killing had not been established.
The suspect was remanded until Nov 3 to facilitate investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
DEATH IN POLICE CUSTODY
The investigation into the
death of 42-year-old Noorizwan Zulkefly,
who died after being detained at the Cheras district police headquarters, became a major police accountability issue during the week.
Noorizwan had been detained to assist investigations into several drug and property offences. He was taken to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz on Sept 30 and pronounced dead the following day.
The circumstances surrounding his death remain under investigation.
On Oct 24, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for a thorough and transparent investigation. On Oct 26, the Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) announced that it had begun investigating alleged misconduct connected with the death.
A forensic medical consultant reported external injuries consistent with blunt-force trauma that were not self-inflicted.
However, police said the complete post-mortem report confirming the cause of death was still pending. Investigators were also working to identify the policemen involved in handling Noorizwan while he was in custody.
Bukit Aman's Criminal Investigation Department has taken over the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loan dispute turns violent in Skudai: Man’s leg broken after being rammed by car, three held
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 31 — A dispute over a loan is believed to have sparked a fight between a group of people outside a supermarket in Taman Pulai Utama, Skudai, which went viral on social media.
Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said police received a report on the incident at 6.38pm yesterday,
Sinar Harian
reported.
He said initial investigations found that the fight broke out between two parties who knew each other before it turned physical.
“In the incident, a 35-year-old local man suffered a broken right leg following an incident involving a car driven by one of the individuals involved.
“The victim received treatment at Hospital Sultanah Aminah (HSA), Johor Baru, and is reported to be in stable condition,” he said in a statement today.
Radin Ramlan said police detained three locals, a man and two women aged between 34 and 53, to assist in investigations.
A Proton Saga was also seized, while police are tracking down several others believed to be involved.
“Urine tests on all three suspects came back negative for drugs, and checks found they have no previous criminal records,” he was quoted as saying.
He said the incident was recorded by a member of the public and uploaded to Facebook.
The case is being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting, which carries a jail term of up to two years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
It is also being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder, which carries a jail term of up to 10 years and a fine, or up to 20 years if hurt is caused.
Radin Ramlan advised the public not to take the law into their own hands to resolve disputes and to refrain from speculating in ways that could disrupt investigations.
Earlier, a 23-second video went viral showing a man, believed to be a motorcyclist, standing on the road with his leg dangling before a Proton Saga rammed into him.
The victim appeared to try to avoid the car but was still hit.
In the footage, a woman can be heard asking the driver why he had hit her husband, to which the driver replied only “balai” (police station).

Title: Supporters out by 7am as Melaka candidates file their papers
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — All 28 nomination centres for the 16th Melaka State Election opened simultaneously at 9 am today.
Prospective candidates have one hour, until 10 am, to submit their nomination papers to the returning officers at their respective centres, after which the list of eligible candidates will be officially announced.
The 14-day campaign period will begin after the announcement of candidates and end at 11.59 pm on November 13.
A Bernama check at several nomination centres found that supporters of various political parties began gathering as early as 7 am to show their support for their respective candidates, with favourable weather conditions reported across the state.
The election is being held following the dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly on September 23, with the consent of the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Melaka, Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10.
A total of 687,697 voters are eligible to cast their ballots in the election, comprising 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
Barisan Nasional (BN) secured 21 seats in the 15th Melaka State Election held on November 20, 2021, with UMNO winning 18, MCA two and MIC one, enabling the coalition to form the state government with a more than two-thirds majority.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats, with DAP securing four and Amanah one, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) took two.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Daylight robbery at a Damansara Damai jeweller, RM300,000 gone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A man armed with a sharp weapon robbed a jewellery shop in Damansara Damai, Petaling Jaya, yesterday afternoon, resulting in losses estimated at RM300,000.
Petaling Jaya district police chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said police were alerted to the robbery at 1.19 pm.
“An investigation paper has been opened under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code, while efforts are underway to track down the suspect,” he said.
Shamsudin urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters operations room at 03-7966 2222 to assist in investigations. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Section 392 of the Penal Code provides the punishment for robbery, while Section 397 applies where the offender uses a deadly weapon, causes grievous hurt, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt. Read together, they carry up to 14 years’ imprisonment, a fine or whipping upon conviction.

Title: Macron to visit Malaysia on Nov 16–17 as ties with France deepen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — French President Emmanuel Macron is expected to visit Malaysia on November 16–17, said Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin.
He said the relationship between Malaysia and France has reached another level following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to France last year, noting that Anwar has established a very good relationship with Macron.
“Datuk Seri Anwar visited France last year and subsequently invited President Macron to visit Malaysia. Macron accepted the invitation within a very short time, and the visit will take place on November 16 and 17, reflecting the growing closeness and strengthening bilateral relationship between the two countries,” he told the media at the Malaysian French Chamber of Commerce & Industry’s (CCIFM) Malaysia-France Gala Night 2026 here today.
He said Malaysia looks forward to Macron’s visit, which will provide an opportunity to further strengthen ties between Malaysian and French companies.
According to him, the bilateral relationship can continue to grow for many more years.
“Malaysia has a very long history with France. In the 1700s, the Sultan of Terengganu invited French traders and seafarers to come to Malaysia to trade.
“Today, we have about 600 French companies operating in Malaysia, including household names such as L’Oréal, Decathlon, Michelin, TotalEnergies and BNP Paribas,” he said.
Meanwhile, in his keynote address during the event, Sim said Malaysia is at advanced stage of negotiations on the Malaysia-European Union Free Trade Agreement (MEUFTA).
“We just concluded one of the negotiations in Brussels, in September.
“I think the discussion is continuing. Recently I received a delegation from Members of Parliament from the European Parliament and we had a further discussion. These are very exciting times for Malaysia and the EU, especially France. I think this is on the right track, in the right direction,” he said.
On October 13, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said Malaysia aims to sign MEUFTA by the end of June 2027, with nearly 80 per cent of negotiations having been completed.
Meanwhile, Ambassador of France to Malaysia, Marc Abensour, said Macron’s upcoming visit to Kuala Lumpur on November 16 and 17 marks an important opportunity to elevate bilateral relations to a strategic partnership.
“This first French presidential visit in nearly a decade will allow us to take our relationship to the next level and to elevate our bilateral relations to the level of strategic partnership, aligning Malaysia with our key regional commitments alongside Indonesia, Singapore, and Vietnam.
“At the core of this relationship is the partnership for sovereignty. In an era where trade, energy, and technology are increasingly weaponised, economic security is paramount. We must secure critical value chains to strengthen our mutual resilience,” he said.
Abensour said both countries are also deepening their longstanding cooperation in defence, aerospace, energy transition, critical minerals and digital infrastructure, including undersea cables, data centres and semiconductors.
“Our economic ties have never been stronger. France is now the second largest European investor in Malaysia, with our investment value growing by 190 per cent over the last decade,” he said.
As it marked its 35th anniversary, CCIFM remains committed to helping French companies establish and expand their operations in the country while leveraging Malaysia as a strategic gateway to Southeast Asia.
Established in 1991, CCIFM has evolved into a key business platform connecting French and Malaysian companies, supporting market entry, facilitating investment and strengthening economic cooperation between the two countries.
Today, more than 600 French companies operate in Malaysia, supporting over 30,000 jobs and contributing to the country’s industrial, technological and economic development.
From aerospace, energy and advanced manufacturing to digital technologies, healthcare and professional services, French companies continue to play an important role in Malaysia’s economic transformation.
Malaysia-France bilateral trade reached RM22.5 billion in 2025. — Bernama

Title: Police probe hacking of Kluang council LED screens after obscene content displayed
Article:
KLUANG, Oct 31 — Eight LED display screens belonging to the Kluang Municipal Council (MPK) around the town are believed to have been hacked to show obscene content on Thursday, according to
Berita Harian
.
Kluang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police received a report on the incident from a 42-year-old local man yesterday.
He said initial investigations found the complainant had been alerted by his staff before receiving several WhatsApp messages containing screenshots and video recordings of the obscene content on the screens.
“Following the incident, the complainant contacted the supplier for confirmation before cutting the power supply to the LED screens to stop the display,” he was quoted as saying.
Bahrin said the case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Computer Crimes Act 1997, which covers unauthorised access with intent to commit a further offence, and Section 292 of the Penal Code over obscene materials.
He said police view the incident seriously and a thorough investigation is under way to identify those involved.
The public has been advised not to speculate or spread unverified information that could disrupt investigations.

Title: AirBorneo launches direct Kuching-Jakarta route from Nov 13, three flights weekly
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 31 — AirBorneo today opened ticket sales for its new direct service between Kuching and Jakarta, with all-in one-way fares starting from RM399 in Economy Class and RM888 in Business Class.
The route to Soekarno-Hatta International Airport will operate three times weekly, on Mondays, Fridays and Sundays, with the inaugural flight scheduled for November 13.
Flight MY 396 departs Kuching at 3.10pm, while the return flight, MY 397, leaves Jakarta at 4.55pm local time.
“Our direct Kuching to Jakarta service marks an important milestone as we grow AirBorneo’s regional network across key Asean gateways,” AirBorneo chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said in a statement.
“A direct link to Indonesia’s commercial capital makes it easier for business leaders, investors and official delegations to travel between our two markets. It also offers patients and families a more comfortable journey to specialist care in Sarawak,” he said.
Megat Ardian added that the route would serve leisure travellers in both directions.
“Indonesian visitors can discover Borneo’s rainforests, culture and festivals, while travellers from Borneo can enjoy all that Jakarta has to offer. We look forward to welcoming them on board with full-service comfort and a taste that’s uniquely Sarawak,” he said.
The state-owned airline also announced its jet network schedule for the Northern Winter 2026/27 season, which runs from October 25 to March 27 next year.
To support the introduction of the Jakarta service, AirBorneo has been operating its Kuching-Singapore service four times weekly since October 23, on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays.
Under the winter schedule, flight MY 0385 departs Kuching at 7.35pm and the return flight, MY 0386, leaves Changi Airport at 10pm.
Passengers holding bookings on affected Singapore services have been contacted directly and offered rebooking options, the airline said.
The twice-daily Kuching-Kuala Lumpur service continues as scheduled, with the afternoon flight MY 5004 now departing Kuala Lumpur at 3.40pm.
AirBorneo said its flights are sold exclusively through verified direct channels to ensure fare transparency, protect consumers against unauthorised third-party markups and provide dedicated customer support.
Established in January 2026 following the transition from MASWings, AirBorneo has expanded beyond Rural Air Services with jet operations, starting with its Kuching-Kuala Lumpur trunk route and growing to include Singapore and Jakarta.

Title: Teen, 14, arrested for throwing stone that shattered KTMB train window in Arau
Article:
ARAU, Oct 31 — A 14-year-old boy has been arrested after admitting to throwing a stone at a Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) train, shattering the window of one of its coaches on Thursday, according to
Sinar Harian
.
The suspect, a local secondary school student, was detained today under Op Cantas by the Arau district Criminal Investigation Division together with the Arau police station task force.
