Arau district police chief Superintendent Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said initial investigations found the suspect had admitted to deliberately throwing a stone at the train while at the Kampung Jelempok motorcycle overpass.
“The suspect also claimed that at the time of the incident, he was hanging out in the area with four of his friends.
“However, only the suspect threw the stone, while his four friends were not involved and merely watched,” he was quoted as saying.
Police had earlier received a report on the incident, in which the window of a KTMB coach was believed to have shattered while the train was travelling from Arau Station towards Alor Setar.
The report was lodged at the Arau police station at 12.30pm yesterday.
Ahmad Mohsin said the suspect was arrested at a house in Kampung Guar Sanji.
He said police also seized a Vivo Y05 mobile phone with a SIM card, as well as a stone believed to be linked to the case.
“The suspect, who has no prior record, is now being held at the Kangar police station lockup to assist investigations,” he said.

Title: Pakatan wants 18 seats in Melaka, and to keep the five it already has
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is targeting victory in 18 of the 24 seats it will contest in the Melaka state election, including retaining the five seats it previously won.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the target was based on an assessment of the coalition’s machinery strength, candidates’ capabilities and the level of public acceptance in the areas it will contest.
“Our target from the outset has been 18 state seats. So, we know that we have the capability to win these 18 seats while working to retain the five seats we currently hold,” he told reporters after the Melaka Media Practitioners’ Hi-Tea in Ayer Keroh here yesterday.
Melaka PKR acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim was also present.
Adly, who is the Bukit Katil incumbent and Deputy Defence Minister, said that of the 24 PH candidates, 10 are from PKR, and seven each from Amanah and DAP.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day on October 31 and early voting on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Seven candidates, seven seats: DAP’s Melaka game plan
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — DAP aims to defend the four seats it currently holds in the 16th Melaka State Election, namely Kesidang, Kota Laksamana, Bandar Hilir and Ayer Keroh.
DAP National Election Director Wong Kah Woh said the party was also eyeing three additional seats allocated to it by Pakatan Harapan (PH), namely Gadek, Duyong and Pengkalan Batu.
The Deputy Education Minister said DAP’s nationwide election machinery would be deployed in phases to assist the party’s seven candidates, with the campaign coordinated by Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong.
“We will do our utmost not only to retain the four seats we won in the previous state election but also to win more this time,” he told reporters here today.
He told reporters this after officiating at the launch of the DAP Kota Laksamana state constituency election operations room, which was also attended by DAP Central Executive Committee member Lim Hui Ying, Khoo, and the party’s Kota Laksamana candidate Low Chee Leong.
Wong said DAP would keep its state-poll campaign positive, focusing on candidates’ performance and service records rather than playing up racial and religious issues.
“We will also highlight Pakatan Harapan’s record of administration at both state and federal levels as one of the foundations for earning voters’ trust,” he said.
He noted that voters in Melaka were increasingly mature in their ability to assess candidates who could represent them and champion their constituencies’ interests.
The Election Commission has set tomorrow as nomination day for the Melaka state election, with polling scheduled for November 14 and early voting on November 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Aini Ideris, UPM’s first woman vice-chancellor, crowned National Academic Figure
Article:
KLANG, Oct 31 — Former Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) vice-chancellor Prof Emeritus Datuk Dr Aini Ideris was named National Academic Figure at the 17th National Academic Awards (AAN) ceremony here yesterday.
The award was presented by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir at a hotel here, with Dr Aini also receiving a trophy, certificate and RM200,000 in prize money.
Dr Aini, 73, has contributed to avian medicine, animal biotechnology and vaccine development, including the development of the Newcastle disease vaccine (NDV4UPM) and a fowlpox vaccine, which have entered international markets.
She also made history as the first woman appointed UPM vice-chancellor, serving from 2016 to 2020, and previously received the 2010 National Academic Award in the Innovation and Product Commercialisation category.
She was also awarded the 2026 Merdeka Award in the Outstanding Contribution to Science, Technology and Innovation category.
The 17th AAN recognised the excellence and contributions of nine academics from higher education institutions (IPTs) in various fields.
The Promising Academic Award went to Prof Dr Ong Wee Jun of Xiamen University Malaysia (XMUM) and Associate Prof Dr Serene Lock Sow Mun of Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP).
The Innovation and Product Commercialisation Award went to Associate Prof Dr Mohd Khairi Abu Husain of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM), while the Book Publication Award was presented to Dr Siti Noor Hafizah Mohamed Sharif of Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).
The Teaching Award (Arts and Social Sciences) went to Associate Prof Dr Saipolbarin Ramli of Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI).
Other recipients were Associate Prof Dr Jayanthi Arasan of UPM for the Teaching Award (Pure Sciences); Dr Ooi Say Keat of USM for the Journal Article Publication Award (Social Sciences and Arts); and Prof Dr Yong Wai Fen of XMUM for the Journal Article Publication Award (Sciences).
Recipients in the respective categories received RM50,000 in prize money, a trophy and a certificate, while the Promising Academic Award recipients received RM25,000.
In his speech, Zambry said the ceremony represented the nation’s highest honour for scholars and academics who had dedicated their lives to advancing knowledge and contributing to society and the country.
“This recognition is not merely an acknowledgement of past achievements, but also a responsibility to continue exploring knowledge, producing quality work and inspiring future generations.
“We want to produce scholars who not only achieve excellence for themselves but also build the greatness of their nation. Scholars can reach for the sky while remaining rooted to the earth,” he said.
The AAN is an annual programme organised by the Higher Education Ministry since 2002. This year’s edition was managed by the Academic Excellence Division of the Department of Higher Education, in collaboration with USM and Universiti Tenaga Nasional (Uniten), which served as the programme’s committee and secretariat. — Bernama

Title: Islamic affairs minister backs making intoxicated drivers pay victims’ families, cites ‘diya’ study can be guide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A study on ‘Diat’ or compensation published by the Federal Territory Mufti’s Office can serve as a reference in detailing compensation payments to victims or next of kin involved in accidents caused by drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the research could provide guidance for proposed amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) to mandate that drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs who cause accidents pay compensation to victims or their heirs.
He said his department fully supports the government’s efforts to amend the act, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027 on October 9.
“Heartiest congratulations to the Federal Territory Mufti’s Office on the publication of the study titled ‘Diya: Understanding and Implementation’. I have also provided a brief explanation to the Transport Minister regarding diya,” he said in an Instagram post yesterday.
On October 12, Transport Minister Anthony Loke stated that his ministry, together with the Attorney General’s Chambers, is currently preparing the policy paper and draft amendments, aiming for tabling during the first session of Parliament next year.
He noted that the proposed mechanism would allow courts to order compensation payments during proceedings against offenders, eliminating the need for victims to file separate civil suits, which can be time-consuming and costly. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: Diya is an Islamic legal term for compensation, traditionally monetary, paid to a victim or the victim’s heirs for death or bodily injury caused by another party.

Title: IGP says ex-border control chief Shuhaily’s PDRM comeback hinges on AGC advice and royal consent
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The new assignment of Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain in the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will only be determined after obtaining the consent of His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia to allow his tenure as Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general to be ended prematurely.
Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said Mohd Shuhaily’s appointment to the post had previously received the consent of His Majesty, as he is a police cadre officer.
In this regard, he said PDRM was awaiting legal advice from the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) before an official letter could be submitted to the King to seek consent for Mohd Shuhaily’s return to the police force.
“Until that consent is granted, I am still waiting. So, I cannot confirm his new assignment status, but he will certainly return to PDRM because he is a police officer,” he told reporters at the 2026 Malaysian Ex-Police Association’s Jasamu Dikenang Dinner held at Kingston Hotel @ Bukit Jalil here tonight.
Commenting further on the duties and follow-up action involving Mohd Shuhaily after his return to PDRM, Mohd Khalid said no decision had been made so far.
“Once he returns to me, we will then consider the next course of action based on the Public Services Commission (SPA). We are civil servants, and all disciplinary matters are subject to the SPA and the Police Force Commission,” he said.
Yesterday, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail confirmed that his ministry had decided last week to return Mohd Shuhaily to PDRM after his secondment to AKPS ended, while leaving the determination of his new assignment to the police leadership.
Mohd Shuhaily was appointed AKPS Director-General for a two-year term from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027.
On October 21, Mohd Shuhaily pleaded not guilty at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court to two charges of causing injury to two police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The abbreviations AKPS stands for Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan Malaysia, SPA stands for Suruhanjaya Perkhidmatan Awam, while PDRM stands for Polis Diraja Malaysia, in Malay.

Title: Nomination day is here: Melaka’s 14-day campaign starts today
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — The 16th Melaka State Election officially begins today, with the nomination process taking place simultaneously at 28 nomination centres across the state from 9 am.
Prospective candidates have until 10 am to submit their nomination papers to the Election Returning Officers before the list of eligible candidates is officially announced.
Following the announcement, the contest for the people’s mandate will enter a 14-day campaigning period, which runs until 11.59 pm on November 13, as stipulated by the Election Commission (EC).
The EC has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10.
It said 189 nomination forms had been purchased as of Thursday night, with 45 prospective candidates having paid their deposits.
EC statistics show that 687,697 people are eligible to vote in the state election, including 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 members of the armed forces and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast clear skies across the state in the morning, setting the scene for a lively nomination day.
The Melaka State Legislative Assembly was officially dissolved with effect from September 23 following the consent of Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional secured 21 of the 28 seats, allowing it to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional took two. — Bernama

Title: Selangor’s Bersatu deal: Just a few ‘sensitive details’ left, says state Pakatan chief
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — A decision regarding the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) between the Selangor State Government and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is expected to be announced in the near future once all negotiation details are finalised.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said that negotiations with Bersatu are ongoing and a foundational understanding has been reached, though several sensitive matters still need to be refined.
He noted that the cooperation established at the Federal level has facilitated efforts to implement a similar approach in Selangor to ensure state administrative stability.
“There are indeed negotiations with Bersatu, and if successful, they will provide en bloc support while remaining as the opposition. The fundamental principles are already in place; it is just that there are a few slightly sensitive details that need to be considered,” he said.
He told reporters this after the Appreciation Ceremony in conjunction with the 22nd Malaysia Games (Sukma) and Para Sukma 2026 at the Raja Muda Musa Hall here yesterday.
Elaborating further, Amirudin said he is ready to finalise the agreement as soon as all related matters are resolved with the party leadership.
“Wait a moment; it is already in place at the Federal level, making it easier for us to implement at the Selangor level. That is indeed the way to ensure cooperation or mutual understanding. Therefore, I am ready for this at any time,” he said.
The proposed implementation of the CSA in Selangor was previously brought forward to ensure smooth state administration – including matters related to the budget – through cross-party cooperation. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The abbreviation Sukma stands for Sukan Malaysia in Malay.

Title: Friends, foes and four awkward clashes: Who’s teaming up with whom in the Melaka polls?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Former rivals Umno and PAS are joining forces to contest the Melaka state election, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu are exploring an electoral understanding — despite preparing to fight each other in four constituencies.
The unusual political arrangements have set the stage for a contest marked by shifting alliances, strained relationships and unfinished electoral deals.
Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) are hoping to repeat their successful cooperation in Negeri Sembilan, where they secured a two-thirds majority in August.
Their seat-sharing negotiations in Melaka have continued right up to nomination day, with MCA securing a fourth constituency following further discussions between the two coalitions.
PH, meanwhile, is seeking common ground with Bersatu even as the latter’s relationship with its PN partners, particularly PAS, continues to deteriorate.
With nominations taking place today ahead of polling on November 14, here is how the alliances are shaping up and what they could mean for Melaka.
BN-PN: United for Melaka
The clearest electoral arrangement in Melaka is between BN, led by Umno, and PN, with PAS playing a central role in the cooperation.
The partnership follows the August 1 Negeri Sembilan state election, where BN and PN agreed not to contest against each other, allowing supporters of either coalition to back a common candidate.
BN won 18 of the 36 seats, while PN secured seven, giving the two coalitions a combined 25 seats and a two-thirds majority in the state assembly. PH, which previously governed the state, was reduced to 11 seats.
The result marked the first electoral success for their cooperation, prompting both coalitions to extend the arrangement to Melaka.
The understanding has since taken shape under the name Muafakat Melaka, bringing together BN, PN and non-governmental organisations in an effort to consolidate support ahead of the election.
Under the seat-sharing arrangement, BN has announced 23 candidates, comprising 18 from Umno, four from MCA and one from MIC.
PN, meanwhile, has named five candidates — two each from PAS and Parti Wawasan Negara, and one from Gerakan.
The arrangement effectively puts Umno and PAS on the same electoral side, allowing both parties to avoid splitting the Malay vote by fielding competing candidates.
It also marks a shift from previous elections, when the two parties contested against each other despite their earlier cooperation under Muafakat Nasional.
For BN, the partnership allows it to retain a larger share of constituencies while benefiting from PAS’ support among conservative Malay voters. For PN, it offers a chance to contest without facing Umno candidates in the same seats.
PH-Bersatu: Allies or rivals?
On the other side, PH has been exploring an electoral understanding with Bersatu under what has been described as PH Plus, although both sides remain at odds over several constituencies.
The discussions emerged amid Bersatu’s deteriorating relationship with its PN partners, particularly PAS, following disagreements over leadership, internal decision-making and electoral cooperation.
Those tensions became more apparent during the Negeri Sembilan election, when Bersatu contested independently rather than joining PN’s seat-sharing arrangement with BN.
Although still associated with PN, Bersatu was excluded from the BN-PN electoral understanding and lost all 24 seats it contested, weakening its electoral position.
Against this backdrop, PH began exploring the possibility of working with Bersatu in Melaka.
On September 19, Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari confirmed that negotiations were being held with parties sharing similar aspirations, including Bersatu, following a decision by the PH Presidential Council to explore wider cooperation.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari subsequently described PH Plus as an electoral understanding rather than a new political coalition, suggesting that any cooperation would be limited to elections rather than a permanent alliance.
Speculation about closer ties gained further attention after Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and several opposition MPs signed a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the federal government on October 29, committing to support Budget 2027.
The agreement also provides for constituency development allocations for Bersatu MPs equivalent to those received by government backbenchers, alongside proposals for institutional reforms.
While the agreement was seen as a possible thaw in relations between Bersatu and the PH-led government, Muhyiddin stressed that it had nothing to do with an electoral pact for the Melaka polls.
Despite the talks and the CSA signing, Bersatu announced eight candidates on Thursday, including four in constituencies also being contested by PH.
The four seats are Klebang, Gadek, Ayer Keroh and Pengkalan Batu.
Bersatu will face PKR in Klebang, while its candidates will go up against DAP in Gadek, Ayer Keroh and Pengkalan Batu.
It will also face PN candidates in Ayer Keroh and Bemban, further highlighting divisions between the former allies.
Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali described the overlapping contests as healthy competition, saying each party had its own considerations when deciding which seats to contest.
He said Bersatu had decided to defend its seats in Sungai Udang and Bemban while targeting other constituencies where it believed it had a chance of winning.
Bersatu has also confirmed that it will use its own party logo in the election.
PH, meanwhile, has expanded its original allocation from 21 to 24 seats, with PKR contesting 10 and DAP and Amanah seven each.
The overlapping contests underline the limits of the proposed PH Plus arrangement, raising questions about how the two sides could reconcile their competing interests should their candidates win seats.
For now, PH and Bersatu appear to be exploring cooperation at a broader political level without a fully coordinated electoral pact in Melaka.
What is at stake in Melaka?
The last Melaka state election in 2021 saw BN secure a commanding victory, winning 21 of the 28 seats, while PH won five and PN two.
However, the state’s federal parliamentary representation paints a different picture.
Of the six parliamentary constituencies covering Melaka, PH and PN each hold three seats, while BN has none.
The contrast highlights the different levels of support enjoyed by the political groupings and the stakes involved in the coming contest.
For BN and PN, the election will test whether their cooperation can translate into stronger support at state level and replicate their success in Negeri Sembilan.
For PH, it presents an opportunity to regain ground after setbacks in recent state elections, while testing whether closer ties with Bersatu could improve its appeal among Malay voters.
Bersatu, meanwhile, faces the challenge of rebuilding its electoral fortunes after its poor showing in Negeri Sembilan, even as it navigates its strained relationship with PN and its tentative understanding with PH.
Analyst predicts commanding BN-PN victory
Political analyst and Nusantara Strategic Research Academy senior fellow Professor Azmi Hassan believes the BN-PN partnership is likely to secure an overwhelming victory, drawing comparisons with the recent elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
He said Malay voters who had previously distanced themselves from PAS or Umno could return in greater numbers now that the two parties were no longer competing against each other.
“Malay voters who previously distanced themselves from PAS or Umno will now come out in droves to support this cooperation. Given that scenario, I think it will be an overwhelming victory for Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional,” he told
Malay Mail
.
Azmi pointed to voting patterns in Johor and, more notably, Negeri Sembilan, where there were indications that PAS supporters had backed Umno candidates in constituencies where the two parties were not competing against each other.
However, he questioned Bersatu’s decision to contest four constituencies against PH despite ongoing discussions between the two sides.
“It’s very odd that Bersatu remains adamant about contesting the four seats where Pakatan Harapan is also fielding candidates,” he said.
Azmi suggested PH could be using the proposed cooperation to test whether Bersatu could help attract Malay voters to its candidates, particularly those from DAP.
“But again, I think Pakatan is testing the waters to see whether cooperation with Bersatu could help attract Malay voters to Pakatan candidates, particularly those from DAP,” he added.
Ultimately, the Melaka election will test whether the BN-PN partnership can repeat its Negeri Sembilan success, while offering an indication of whether PH’s efforts to widen its electoral cooperation can help it regain ground among Malay voters.

Title: Malaysian doctor Mary Suma Cardosa makes history as first Asian to lead global pain research body
Article:
BANGKOK, Oct 30 — Malaysian physician Dr Mary Suma Cardosa has made history as the first Asian to become president of the International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) in the organisation’s more than 50-year history.
Cardosa assumed the two-year presidency, which runs until 2028, at the closing of the 2026 World Congress on Pain in Bangkok on Friday, succeeding Andrew Rice of the United Kingdom.
In a statement issued by IASP, she said her presidency would focus on advancing pain science, strengthening healthcare education and improving access to effective pain management worldwide.
“Pain affects people in every country, but access to effective pain care remains profoundly unequal,” she said, highlighting the importance of education, stronger clinical services and multidisciplinary cooperation.
An anaesthesiologist with more than three decades of experience in pain medicine, Cardosa has played a pivotal role in developing Malaysia’s pain management services and strengthening pain education in the country and across Southeast Asia.
Her contributions include establishing the Health Ministry’s first acute pain service in 1993 and the country’s first multidisciplinary pain clinic in 2000.
She also spearheaded Malaysia’s Pain Free Hospital initiative, launched in 2011 to improve pain recognition and management in healthcare facilities.
Cardosa previously made history in 2011 as the first woman to serve as president of the Malaysian Medical Association.
Beyond Malaysia, Cardosa has contributed to regional and international initiatives to expand pain-care capacity, including training healthcare professionals and supporting the development of multidisciplinary services in resource-limited countries.
As IASP president, she will lead the association’s global efforts to advance pain research and translate scientific knowledge into better patient care, alongside the implementation of its 2026-2030 Strategic Plan.
IASP is a leading international organisation dedicated to the study of pain and the translation of scientific knowledge into improved pain relief worldwide. It brings together scientists, clinicians, healthcare professionals, and policymakers to advance pain research, education, and care. — Bernama

Title: Paws off! Shah Alam High Court rules condo management cannot impose blanket pet bans
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 30 — The High Court here today ruled that a joint management body (JMB) cannot impose a blanket ban on keeping pets in private residential units through its house rules.
In a statement, lawyers Rajesh Nagarajan and Sachpreetraj Singh Sohanpal, who represented former national hurdler Noraseela Mohd Khalid, said the court partially allowed her application against the JMB of Shang Villa Condominium, declaring that House Rule 9.0 could not be used to prohibit her from keeping her three cats in her residential unit.
They said the court ruled that the mere presence of pets in a residential unit did not constitute a breach of house rules and that any enforcement action must be based on By-law 14 of the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015 and supported by evidence.
“The court decided that there is no blanket prohibition. House Rule 9.0 cannot be used to prohibit or penalise Ms Noraseela merely for keeping her three cats; Enforcement must be evidence-based.
“There must be a factual basis connecting the particular animal to an alleged nuisance, danger or other prohibited circumstance,” the statement said.
The lawyers said the court also found that general complaints about animals were insufficient, as the evidence did not establish that Noraseela’s cats were responsible for the incidents cited by the JMB.
They said evidence from a neighbour supported Noraseela’s account that the cats were properly cared for, while veterinary certificates indicated that they were in good health.
The court also declared invalid and unenforceable the provisions of House Rule 9.0 that allowed animals to be removed from common property without notifying their owners and excluded liability for any resulting loss, insofar as they bypassed the requirements, notice procedures and safeguards under By-law 14.
“This judgment confirms that a JMB is not above the law. House rules cannot be used to circumvent statutory safeguards or to create powers the legislation does not confer. The law regulates irresponsible conduct. It does not authorise discrimination against responsible pet owners.
“Legitimate complaints about animals must be addressed, and this decision does not stand in the way of that. But management must act on evidence, not on a presumption that every pet is a nuisance,” the statement said.
In a document shared with the media, Noraseela, in her application contested the validity of House Rule 9.0, arguing that it contradicted the Strata Management Act 2013 (SMA 2013), which allows residents to keep pets subject to reasonable regulations to prevent nuisance, danger or annoyance.
She argued that Section 70(2) of the Act prohibited house rules that were inconsistent with its provisions, while Section 150 did not empower the Joint Management Body (JMB) to impose a blanket ban on pets but only to regulate their keeping for management purposes.
Noraseela therefore contended that House Rule 9.0 was unlawful and invalid as it went beyond the powers provided under the Act.
She also argued that the blanket ban under House Rule 9.0 was excessive and disproportionate as it applied to all residents without requiring evidence of nuisance or harm, claiming that it violated the principle of proportionality under Article 8 of the Federal Constitution and interfered with her right to enjoy and use her property under Article 13. — Bernama

Title: RM3 for extra soup? Labuan eatery compounded for failing to display charge on menu
Article:
LABUAN, Oct 30 — An eatery operator here was compounded after charging an additional RM3 for a serving of soup that was not listed on the restaurant’s displayed price menu.
KPDN Labuan director Junaidah Arbain said the action followed a consumer complaint lodged through the ministry’s e-Aduan portal, with an inspection at about 10am finding that the displayed price list included additional charges for rice and noodles but did not specify the price of extra soup.
“Following the non-compliance detected, we issued a compound to the operator under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking for Goods and Charges for Services) Order 2020, under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011,” she told Bernama today.
Junaidah said individuals convicted of an offence under the order could be fined up to RM50,000, while companies could face fines of up to RM100,000.
She reminded restaurant and food outlet operators to display their menus and all additional charges completely, clearly and prominently, with price lists and charges stated in Bahasa Melayu or accompanied by a translation if presented in another language, and prices indicated in ringgit or sen.
She said that transparent pricing was essential to protecting consumer rights, as customers were entitled to know the cost of goods and services before placing an order or making a purchase.
“KPDN Labuan would continue to intensify enforcement and monitoring activities to safeguard consumer interests, and members of the public are encouraged to report business-related non-compliance through the ministry’s official complaint channels,” she added. — Bernama

Title: Foreign investments should deliver more opportunities for Malaysian SMEs, says Steven Sim
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The government wants local content to be given greater consideration in government, government-linked company (GLC) and multinational corporation (MNC) procurements to create more opportunities for local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said the approach is aimed at ensuring local businesses benefit from investments and the development of domestic supply chains.
“We also want government procurements, GLC procurements and, of course, MNC procurements to have a perspective for local content. We want foreign direct investment (FDI) to come in to benefit local businesses. So, there must be a requirement for local contents,” he said.
He said this during a panel discussion with Grant Thornton Malaysia National Tax Practice Leader Datin Seah Siew Yun at the Grant Thornton Tax Seminar on Budget 2027 here today.
Sim said local content requirement is one of the components under the SCALE Action Plan, which will form the ministry’s next phase of longer-term structural reforms for the MSME sector.
He said SCALE covers SME redefinition, cash flow protection, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, local content requirement and easing access to financing, with the ministry looking at reforms through legislation, regulation or policy.
On FDI, Sim said the government has also retweaked its investment incentive system under the new incentive framework, with tax incentives linked to key performance indicators (KPIs).
Among the criteria are the creation of high-paying jobs for Malaysians and development of the local supply chain, with the approach intended to ensure foreign investments generate spillover benefits for MSMEs instead of benefitting only large companies.
Meanwhile, Sim said GLCs and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) have an important role in developing local industries and helping smaller businesses grow, while avoiding crowding them out of the market.
He said the government has instructed GLCs and GLICs to invest up to RM25 billion annually to develop the local supply chain, adding that part of the funds should be invested domestically to build local industries.
Sim said strengthening MSMEs is crucial as they account for about 96 per cent of business establishments in Malaysia, although their contribution to gross domestic product (GDP) remains below 40 per cent.
He said the government is targeting MSMEs to contribute at least 40 per cent to GDP, noting that while SMEs similarly make up an overwhelming majority of business establishments in many developed economies, their economic contribution is higher. — Bernama

Title: Eleventh-hour boost for MCA: Perikatan returns Kota Laksamana, bringing Melaka seat tally to four
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — MCA has announced that it will contest one more state seat in the 16th Melaka state election, after Kota Laksamana was returned to Barisan Nasional (BN) by Perikatan Nasional (PN).
MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said Melvin Chua will be fielded as the candidate, following discussions between BN and PN after the latter indicated that MCA is better suited to contest the seat.
“This decision was only made and agreed upon today by the party’s top leadership, following the decision to return the seat to an MCA candidate representing BN in the Kota Laksamana state constituency, after taking into consideration his suitability based on his involvement and services in the area,” he told a press conference during a visit to the Bandar Hilir MCA operations room in Melaka Raya here today.
Wee said Melvin is a familiar figure among the local community, particularly through his involvement in community activities and his service in the Melaka Historic City Council (MBMB) administrative area.
The addition of Kota Laksamana means MCA will contest four seats, including Machap Jaya, Kelebang and Bandar Hilir.
Wee said the latest development would not affect MCA’s preparations, despite the decision being made at the last minute, as the party had long been prepared, particularly in the traditional constituencies it was contesting.
He said MCA, as BN’s component party, is ready to face any challenge and has no problem fielding candidates in seats where it is required to contest.
“We have never shied away from our responsibilities. We have no problem contesting any seat and we are ready to face any situation.
“MCA will continue striving to gain the people’s support and put up a fight in the constituencies it contests, including seats considered difficult to win in the Melaka state polls,” he said.
The Election Commission has fixed tomorrow as nomination day for the Melaka state election, with polling set for November 14 and early voting on November 10. — Bernama

Title: Sabah defence upgrades not a response to Philippine military build-up, says Khaled
Article:
LABUAN, Oct 30 — Malaysia will continue strengthening its military capabilities in Sabah to safeguard national security amid regional geopolitical developments, but the move is not a direct response to the Philippines’ military build-up on Balabac Island, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
He said every country has the right to enhance its defence capabilities, and Malaysia was similarly committed to ensuring its armed forces remained prepared for any potential escalation of regional tensions.
“Every country has the right to strengthen its military capabilities, and Malaysia will do the same. However, our efforts are not a reaction to what the Philippines is doing in its southern region, but part of our preparations to ensure that any escalation of tensions will have minimal impact on Malaysia,” he told reporters after receiving the FA-50M aircrafts from South Korea at the Labuan Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base here.
Khaled was commenting on the Philippine government’s efforts to strengthen military facilities on Balabac Island in southern Palawan, which has been designated as a military cooperation site accessible to the United States forces.
Khaled said strengthening Malaysia’s defence capabilities, particularly in Sabah, remained a key priority of the Defence Ministry.
He said the ministry would determine the number of FA-50M light combat aircraft to be stationed at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base in Labuan following the planned decommissioning of Hawk fighter aircraft in 2028.
“Once the Hawk aircraft are phased out in 2028, we will determine how many FA-50M aircraft will be stationed at the Labuan air base,” he said.
He said the government had also decided to install new radar systems in Sabah, including on Layang-Layang Island, to enhance surveillance and early detection capabilities.
“The ministry would also increase military personnel in Sabah, where more than 10,000 troops are currently stationed, while new military camps have been developed to strengthen operational readiness,” he said.
Khaled reiterated that the initiatives were part of Malaysia’s continuing efforts to reinforce national defence and protect its sovereignty, rather than a response to military developments in neighbouring countries. — Bernama

Title: The more, the merrier? State Pakatan chairman says crowded Melaka races could work in coalition’s favour
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) does not regard multi-cornered contests in the Melaka state election as a disadvantage, saying a crowded field could instead create more opportunities for the coalition to secure victories.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said a straight fight did not necessarily give a party an advantage, as three- or four-cornered contests could, in certain circumstances, offer better prospects from a strategic standpoint.
“Based on my experience in previous four-cornered contests, having more candidates is not necessarily an obstacle to winning. Instead, it can create opportunities that contesting parties can take advantage of.
“There are certainly challenges as well as advantages in terms of our strategy. Sometimes, a straight fight can be more difficult than a three-cornered contest,” he told reporters after a tea reception with Melaka media practitioners in Ayer Keroh here today.
Also present was Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim.
Adly said PH’s decision to increase the number of seats it is contesting from 21 to 24 was also made after assessing the current political landscape and the coalition’s prospects of winning.
He said the coalition had initially settled on contesting 21 seats on October 24 before reviewing its position and identifying further opportunities to strengthen its chances.
The decision, he said, should not be interpreted as a failure in negotiations with any political party, as PH had made its assessment based on its own capabilities and prevailing political developments.
He said another principle taken into consideration was to ensure that no state constituency was won uncontested, allowing voters to exercise their democratic right to choose their representatives.
“For example, when we realised that Bersatu was not fielding a candidate in a particular seat, that decision had been made without consulting us.
“So we stepped in to ensure the democratic process could proceed as it should. Voters must be given the opportunity to make their choice,” he said.
Nominations will take place tomorrow, with early voting on November 10 and polling on November 14. — Bernama

Title: MOF never ordered rural road projects cancelled, only deferred new contracts, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) has never issued any directive to cancel rural road projects, but has only deferred new contracts to prevent outstanding payments to contractors from continuing to accumulate, according to the prime minister’s senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz.
He said the deferment was necessary following rural road development expenditure exceeding the original allocations approved by Parliament annually since 2022, resulting in increased contractual commitments and outstanding payments to contractors.
“The deferment of new contracts does not mean existing projects have been cancelled. MOF has never issued any directive to cancel projects. New contracts were deferred to prevent outstanding payments from continuing to increase.
“These are two different things. That is why the country’s finances must be managed prudently, not merely by approving projects but also by ensuring sufficient allocations are available to pay for them,” he said in a video shared on his social media today.
Tengku Zafrul said claims that rural road allocations, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, had been deliberately reduced should be assessed based on the government’s actual expenditure figures for the period concerned.
He said rural road expenditure for the 2023-2027 period, including allocations for this year and next year, had increased to RM11 billion compared with RM3.7 billion for the 2018-2022 period, representing almost a threefold increase.
“In Sabah and Sarawak alone, actual rural road expenditure this year reached RM1.41 billion, the highest in the past 10 years.
“Since 2023, RM4.6 billion has been spent. Every year, approximately half of the country’s total rural road expenditure is channelled to Sabah and Sarawak. Sabah and Sarawak have not been sidelined. Sabah and Sarawak have been given priority,” he said.
Tengku Zafrul said MOF had to balance the allocation needs of all ministries, including those responsible for health, education and rural development, to ensure the government’s financial commitments could be met.
He said when a ministry made spending commitments that exceeded its approved allocation, MOF had to seek additional financial resources to meet those requirements.
In this regard, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had approved an additional RM500 million in expenditure for 2026, using savings from the development allocations of other ministries, to enable outstanding payments to contractors to be settled.
He said the government understood that many villages in Sabah and Sarawak were still waiting for better road facilities.
In this connection, Budget 2027 provides RM2.27 billion for rural road development, while RM34.9 billion has been allocated to Sabah and Sarawak, the highest amount among all states.
He also reminded all parties that development issues in the two states should not be used as political ammunition.
“As the prime minister has stressed, allocations alone are not enough without good governance. What matters is that projects are implemented, contractors are paid and the people benefit. That is our priority,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Saris, sweets and shopping sprees: Deepavali buzz builds across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The festive atmosphere ahead of Deepavali on November 8 is becoming more vibrant as the Indian community nationwide begins making preparations for the Festival of Lights, including purchasing traditional attire, preparing special delicacies and decorating their homes to celebrate the occasion with family and relatives.
Bernama’s survey in several states found that shopping hotspots are beginning to draw crowds purchasing festive essentials, while traders are offering a wide selection of goods and special promotions to attract customers.
In
KUALA LUMPUR
, traders in Little India, Brickfields, are hoping for an increase in visitors this weekend, although the recent unpredictable weather has somewhat affected sales.
Shoe and accessories trader Vishan Daren, 30, said the rain had resulted in fewer customers, but visitor numbers have started to pick up today and are expected to increase further on Saturday and Sunday.
In
SELANGOR
, a survey at Little India, Klang, found that Deepavali preparations had also attracted people from various ethnic communities, including Nadia Dastghill, 44, who was shopping for traditional Indian attire for her child’s school celebration and a sari as a gift for the teacher.
Another visitor, N. Rama Rao, 38, said Little India remains his family’s preferred shopping destination as it offers a wide selection of traditional attire at reasonable prices.
Deepavali preparations are gathering pace in Ipoh, with traders hoping for a rise in customers over the weekend. — Bernama pic
In
NEGERI SEMBILAN
, about 30,000 visitors are expected to throng the Deepavali Bazaar at Jalan Datuk Lee Fong Yee, popularly known as Little India Seremban, throughout its 10-day operation, which began yesterday.
Negeri Sembilan Indian Community Affairs special officer Datuk VS Mogan said the bazaar features 140 traders offering a variety of festive goods, as well as performances by local artistes, including Santesh Kumar, to enliven the atmosphere.
In
JOHOR
, members of the public have begun making early preparations by visiting the Deepavali Bazaar along Jalan Ungku Puan in Johor Bahru to purchase traditional attire, decorative flowers, accessories, as well as various sweets and snacks.
Homemaker K. Kalaivani, 40, from Pasir Gudang, said she chose to shop a week in advance to avoid the last-minute crowds.
Meanwhile, traditional snack trader Renuka, 34, said customer response has been encouraging so far, with tarts,
suji
and
murukku
among the most sought-after festive delicacies.
Shoppers browse traditional attire, accessories and festive decorations ahead of Deepavali in Johor Bahru October 30, 2026. — Bernama pic
In
PENANG
, the festive excitement ahead of Deepavali is evident, with business premises adorned with colourful decorations and offering special sales and discounts on selected items.
VKN Sivasamy & Son director Aditya Tandian said customer response is almost on par with last year’s, with some visitors coming from Sungai Petani, Kulim, Ipoh and Kuala Lumpur, while about 10 to 15 per cent of customers made their purchases online.
In
PERLIS
, V. Malarvizhi, 56, a vendor selling festive goods in Pauh, Arau, said customer response remains slow but is expected to pick up about a week before Deepavali, as people begin shopping for clothes, religious items and traditional delicacies.
Malarvizhi, who has been in the business for more than 10 years, said most customers typically made their purchases in the final week before the festival, while she would make her own preparations three to four days before Deepavali.
Colourful ‘saris’, ‘kurtas’ and festive accessories are among the goods attracting shoppers ahead of the Festival of Lights. — Bernama pic
In
PAHANG
, Dr S. Bavani, 43, from Kuantan, said her family’s preparations begin with purchasing traditional attire such as
saris
and
kurtas
, as well as preparing traditional delicacies, including
murukku
and sweets, to serve guests.
The mother of two said cleaning and decorating the house with oil lamps and colourful ornaments are also part of the preparations to create a festive atmosphere.
Meanwhile, in
KELANTAN
, the Hindu community in Kuala Krai and Tanah Merah is making modest preparations while maintaining traditions such as preparing festive delicacies, cleaning their homes and strengthening family and neighbourhood ties.
Single mother of seven, R. Parvathy, 68, from Kuala Krai, said her children helped purchase traditional attire and other festive necessities, while she prepared
murukku
to be shared with family members and neighbours.
Another Tanah Merah resident, S. Chandrakala, 40, said preparing traditional delicacies such as murukku and laddu with family members not only added to the festive cheer but also ensured that the heritage continued to be preserved by younger generations. — Bernama
Traditional Deepavali delicacies, including ‘murukku’, ‘laddu’ and ‘suji’, are among the popular purchases as families prepare for the celebrations. — Bernama pic

Title: Rubbish raid! Thirteen-foot crocodile caught after rummaging through trash for food in Sarawak village
Article:
KOTA SAMARAHAN, Oct 30 — A crocodile measuring over 13 feet (about 3.96m) was captured this morning following reports of the reptile roaming in the area and posing a potential safety concern for nearby villagers.
Licensed crocodile capture team Sarawak Crocter said in a Facebook post that the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC).
“The crocodile has gone viral recently and has now been captured for the sake of the villagers’ safety.
“Please report any dangerous crocodile sightings to the authorities as soon as possible,” the post read.
Meanwhile, licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew said in a separate post that the reptile had been spotted in the area two days earlier, rummaging through rubbish for food. — The Borneo Post

Title: Bought one thing, got another? Anwar orders crackdown on online shopping scams, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), to take immediate action against fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive followed Anwar’s concerns over problems faced by online shoppers and sellers, including high commission fees imposed on merchants and customers receiving products that did not match their orders.
“The prime minister raised concerns about the problems faced by e-commerce users, particularly high fees and commissions charged to sellers, as well as customers receiving products that differ from what they ordered.
“He has therefore instructed KPDN and the Communications Ministry, particularly through MCMC, to take action on several issues, especially fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms,” he told a press conference after the Cabinet meeting here today.
He said MCMC had met representatives of all major e-commerce platforms several weeks ago to discuss the issues.
Fahmi said that a retreat involving enforcement agencies would be held in the coming weeks to coordinate an integrated response to problems affecting e-commerce users.
“The prime minister has directed that this matter be prioritised and addressed urgently.
“Insya-Allah, I will make several additional announcements on the issue tomorrow during the National Courier Day celebration,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sale of first industrial plots on Silicon Island to start in Q1 2027, says Penang CM
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The Penang government hopes to sell the first industrial plots on Silicon Island as early as the first quarter of 2027, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the development on Silicon Island will focus on the 700-acre Green Tech Park which is planned as a green, smart and sustainable high-tech industrial hub in line with environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles.
“The sale of the first industrial plots is expected to begin as early as the first quarter of 2027 to attract high-value investments, particularly in the semiconductor, automated test equipment, integrated circuit design and medical device sectors,” he said when tabling the Supply Bill at the state legislative assembly today.
He said the first factory in the Green Tech Park is expected to begin operations by 2028 while creating high-skilled employment opportunities for Penangites.
“The development of Silicon Island is not merely about providing new land for industry, but is also a long-term investment that generates benefits for the local economy,” he said.
He said a total of 4,531 contracts worth RM1.92 billion had been awarded to local contractors and businesses as of September 30.
On the development of Silicon Island, he said a total of 500 acres had been reclaimed, equivalent to 39.4 per cent of the 1,270-acre Phase 1 as of October.
In May this year, he said a 64.85-acre site was also prepared for the Mutiara Line LRT depot.

Title: Repairs on Kuching’s Jalan Lapangan Terbang water main completed, supply restoration in stages, says Sarawak Water
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 30 — Emergency repair works on a critical 750mm mild steel cement-lined (MSCL) water main on Jalan Lapangan Terbang were completed at 2am today, said Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd.
The utility provider said water supply restoration is now underway in stages.
It said the unscheduled water supply interruption was necessitated by repair works on the 750mm pipeline located off Jalan Kuching Ranger Depot after it was damaged by third-party operations associated with the Kuching Urban Transportation System (KUTS) project.
The disruption affected consumers in the Datuk Muda Tank supply area, Jalan Lapangan Terbang, Jalan Tun Jugah, Jalan Batu Lintang, and surrounding areas.
The company had initially estimated the interruption to last from 4.30pm on October 29 until 5am on October 30.
In a progress update issued at 11.45pm yesterday, the utility provider said the leak location had been identified and repair crews were dewatering the site to facilitate repair works.
Following completion of the repair works at 2am, Sarawak Water said valve reopening and network pressurisation had commenced, with water supply expected to be restored gradually.
Consumers in higher-elevation areas or those located towards the end of distribution lines may experience a longer delay before normal water pressure is fully restored.
The company also cautioned that consumers might temporarily experience discoloured or muddy water, as well as milky-looking water, when supply resumed.
It explained that sediment dislodged from the pipelines could cause temporary discolouration, while trapped air bubbles could give the water a milky appearance.
Consumers are advised to run their external taps for a few minutes until the water becomes completely clear before using it for cooking, drinking, or washing.
Sarawak Water also advised consumers in the affected areas to use water wisely and thanked residents and businesses for their patience and understanding throughout the emergency repair operation.
The utility provider said it would continue monitoring the distribution system as water supply recovery progresses. — The Borneo Post

Title: Penang Budget 2027 sets aside RM600 aid for e-hailing drivers, RM500 for newlyweds
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — E-hailing drivers will be getting a special one-off incentive of RM600 in 2027 under the newly tabled state Budget 2027.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the special incentive is in recognition of the welfare of those working in the public transport sector.
“This is for eligible drivers in 2027 with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million,” he said when tabling the Supply Bill at the state legislative assembly today.
He said there will also be an allocation of RM1.2 million for taxi drivers and school bus operators in 2027.
As for the incentives for newlyweds, he said the Mempelai Emas programme is an expansion of the i-Sejahtera programme as a form of appreciation for couples who have recently married in Penang.
“Couples who meet the eligibility requirements will receive a one-off contribution of RM500,”  he said.
He said the state government had disbursed RM57.8 million through the implementation of the first and second phases of the i-Sejahtera programme as at September 30.
The programme benefited a total 299,504 recipients, particularly senior citizens, persons with disabilities, single mothers and housewives.
He added that the addition of the Mempelai Emas programme is also included in the state’s annual allocation of RM58 million for the i-Sejahtera programme in 2027.
Meanwhile, he said the state government is also examining changes in the structure of society and current housing needs.
He said there is a growing need for housing involving single people and senior citizens living alone.
“As such, in 2027, the Penang State Housing Board (LPNPP) will explore the co-living concept for suitable state government rental housing and People’s Housing Programme units,” he said.
Chow said the state will be introducing a Penang State Social Development Fund for the first time in 2027 with an allocation of RM350,000.
“The fund will support the implementation of various welfare and social development initiatives, particularly to assist those in need, address poverty and social inequality, and empower vulnerable groups so that they are not left behind in the state’s development,” he said.

Title: Indonesian woman fined RM4,000 and ordered deported over RM100 sex offer to undercover cop in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 30 — An Indonesian woman was fined RM4,000 in default six months in jail by the Magistrates’ Court here for soliciting sexual services from an undercover policeman for RM100.
Magistrate Nureina Syafika Mohd Najib imposed the sentence against Pita, 37, after she pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 372B of the Penal Code.
According to the charge, Pita committed the offence at a beauty and health centre on Jalan Batu Kawa here at around 5pm on October 27.
Based on the facts of the case, police conducted an inspection at the premises to detect prostitution activities following information received from an undercover police agent, who had been instructed to carry out the operation.
During the inspection of an unnumbered room, police found Pita with the undercover agent and arrested her for further action.
Items seized to assist for the investigation included a bottle of massage oil, an unused condom, a packet of wet wipes, and RM100.
Investigations found that Pita had offered sexual services to the undercover agent for a cash payment of RM100.
Pita also pleaded guilty to an immigration offence for being in Malaysia without a valid pass, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Judge Mursyida Abd Halim sentenced her to four months in prison, effective October 30 and ordered that she be deported to her home country upon completion of her sentence.
The two charges were prosecuted separately by deputy public prosecutors Ahmad Fauzulutfi Suriani and Marvind Kaliyani.
Pita did not have legal representation. — The Borneo Post
